I didn't mean to pick at you. When fluent English speakers read, "<some nation> Special Forces," that is taken to mean that the country's military has deployed special forces/commandos to deal with the demonstrators. That's why the article was careful say Police Special Forces. Those sorts of policemen have labels like "Special Weapons And Tactic" Team, Crisis Response Force, Riot Police, Armed Response Teams, etc... The names vary by municipality/country.

Word choice can be very hard when English is not a first language. There are so many words that sound alike, or have identical spellings, yet their meanings differ according to which syllable is stressed... So many pitfalls. Then there are all the regional usage issues (dialectics) that change the meaning of certain words.

Anyway, that is why I thought your title was misleading.
